{{Quote|Aunt Beru always brought a good idea and a cool drink out when she came to visit her men. And when they became frustrated, she had words of encouragement that got them going again.|Camie Loneozner|<ref name="Camie's Story">{{WEGCite|story=Camie's Story|book=Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope}}</ref>}}
'''Beru Whitesun Lars''', the wife of [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]], was a [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooinian]] woman who raised [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] after the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Coming from a long line of [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmers]], Beru Whitesun grew up near [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on Tatooine. On a trip to [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]], she met Owen Lars, the son of another moisture farmer, [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]]. Beru and Owen fell in love, and Beru later became part of the [[Lars family/Legends|Lars family]].

Shortly before the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Owen's stepmother, [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker Lars]], was kidnapped by [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]], an event that brought Shmi's son, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], and his soon-to-be-wife, [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], to the [[Lars homestead/Legends|Lars homestead]]. Three years later, when the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflict came to a close, Beru and Owen became the guardians of their new baby nephew, Luke Skywalker, after his father turned to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] and became Darth Vader.

The Larses raised Skywalker. Beru would often defend Skywalker against Owen. Owen refused numerous times to let Skywalker go when he wished to leave the farm to attend the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] with his friend [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]], Beru convinced her husband to let Luke go after one more season. After a year had passed, Beru tried to convince Owen that it was time to let Skywalker move on, as he was still reluctant to do so. They never had time to reach an agreement. The two were killed by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], by order of Darth Vader, who were searching for a [[R2-D2/Legends|droid]] carrying the stolen [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
Growing up near the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]],<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /> Beru Whitesun was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> born in [[47 BBY/Legends|47 BBY]].<ref name="ff140" /> Her siblings, [[Dama Whitesun Brunk|Dama]] and [[Haro Whitesun|Haro]], and she came from a [[Whitesun family|family]] that had been in the [[Moisture farm/Legends|moisture farming]] businesses for three generations.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /><ref name="Star Wars Galaxies" /><ref name="Coolie">In [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Luke mentions having an "Aunt [[Coolie]]." Since Luke's only real aunts were [[Sola Naberrie/Legends|Sola Naberrie]] and Beru, Coolie was probably either another sister of Beru or perhaps a close friend.</ref> The Whitesuns had a reputation among the [[Farm/Legends|farming]] families for being particularly well-adapted to Tatooine's rough climate.<ref name="Databank">{{DB|character|berulars|Lars, Beru}}</ref>

===The Lars family===
{{Quote|We Lars men fall in love with the best women.|[[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones (novel)">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Young_Owen_and_Beru.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Beru and Owen meet Anakin Skywalker.]]
Not long before the onset of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Whitesun met a young man in [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]] named [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]]. Lars, also a moisture farmer, lived on a [[Lars homestead/Legends|farm]] with his father, [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]], and stepmother, [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker Lars]]. Whitesun developed a romantic relationship with Owen, and also grew close to his [[Lars family/Legends|family]]. Her sister, Dama, would accompany her on visits to the Lars farm, although she would often leave for Anchorhead to visit a beau of her own.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /> While Owen and Whitesun had not yet announced that they were getting [[Marriage/Legends|married]], Shmi could tell that it would only be a matter of time before they would wed. She knew that Whitesun's strong work ethic and easy-going nature would make her a good wife for a moisture farmer. Likewise, Cliegg found a strong verbal sparring partner in Whitesun; she held her own in playfully arguing with "old Cliegg."<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones (novel)" />

Whitesun was staying with the Larses for a few [[Standard day/Legends|days]] when a group of [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] and their [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]] began approaching the perimeter of the farm.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /> While Cliegg and Owen tried to convince the women that there was nothing to worry about, Beru and Shmi saw through their lies and demanded to hear the truth. The family then prepared for the oncoming attack. When Shmi was kidnapped by the Tuskens, Cliegg and Owen recruited other local farmers to help them [[Battle of Great Chott|go after]] the Sand People. Many men were killed, and Cliegg lost his right leg, but Shmi was never recovered. Two [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] after she was taken, Whitesun and the Larses tearfully accepted that Shmi was gone.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones (novel)" />

[[File:Kitster.png|thumb|Kitster Banai, a friend of Skywalker's who Beru shared stories with.]]
A [[Standard month/Legends|month]] passed since Shmi's kidnapping. Whitesun was surprised when she finally got the chance to meet [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], the son Shmi so often spoke of, when the [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] and he arrived on Tatooine to see his mother. While Cliegg explained what had happened, Whitesun prepared food and drinks for the guests. She was at Cliegg's when Skywalker set out to find Shmi, and she was the first to spot him on his return from the [[Valley of the Spirits|Tusken camp]]. When he arrived, she stood next to Owen and sadly watched as Anakin carried his mother's [[Death/Legends|lifeless]] body into their house. She later helped Amidala prepare a meal for the distraught Skywalker; she asked Amidala what it was like on her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], but confessed that she preferred Tatooine and didn't like to travel.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones (novel)" />

Beru and the others held a [[Funeral of Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|funeral]] for Shmi, and buried her body on the western edge of the sand berm near the house.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /> Skywalker and Amidala departed Tatooine, taking [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], a droid who had been with the Larses as long as Shmi, along with them.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref> Shortly thereafter, [[Kitster Chanchani Banai|Kitster Banai]], a childhood friend of Skywalker's, came to the farm hoping to see his friend. Instead, Beru shared with him the story of the recent events.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

===Raising Luke===
{{Quote|Luke's just not a farmer, Owen. He has too much of his father in him.|Beru Lars|<ref name="A New Hope" />}}
[[File:Beru_Luke.png|thumb|200px|Beru receives baby Luke.|left]]
Three years went by, over which time Whitesun and Owen had married, and Cliegg had died and left the farm to them.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /><ref name="[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> Mere days after the Clone Wars came to an end and Anakin Skywalker [[Showdown on Coruscant|became Darth Vader]], the Larses spoke to the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'' junior novel]]</ref> Kenobi asked them to become the guardians of their nephew, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], simply telling them that Skywalker's parents were dead, and not giving any details as to how.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)" /> Although Owen was initially reluctant, the pair agreed after Beru convinced her husband to adopt the boy.<ref name="SWCE">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Despite the Larses raising the child, Kenobi would live [[Ben Kenobi's home/Legends|nearby]] on Tatooine to keep an eye on Skywalker.<ref name="The Last One Standing">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing|book=Legacy of the Jedi/Secrets of the Jedi omnibus|text=''Legacy of the Jedi/Secrets of the Jedi'' omnibus}}</ref> The Larses told their neighbors that they had given him the name "Skywalker" to honor Owen's late stepmother.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

The Larses took Luke in and raised him. On the farm, Beru often carried baby Skywalker with her on a sling while she would gather [[Vaporator mushroom/Legends|mushrooms]] that grew on the [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporators]]; Owen would always go with her for protection. On one particular morning, the Larses discovered that Tusken Raiders had stolen roughly a third of their vaporators. Kenobi, who frequently checked on the Larses from afar, noticed this and approached the homestead. Beru insisted that they leave the Tuskens alone, fearing for the life of her husband, but Owen felt that the local farmers and he should go after them again. However, Kenobi took the initiative himself. He went to the Tusken camp and retrieved the vaporators, returning them to the Larses that night. Beru had mixed emotions; she was glad that Owen would not have to fight, but she did not want to be indebted to Kenobi.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /> Still, he would [[Duel on Tatooine (Imperial Period)|defend]] the family from Tuskens again, this time from a raiding party led by a former Jedi, [[Darth Krayt|A'Sharad Hett]].<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 16: Claws of the Dragon, Part 3">[[Legacy (2006) 16|''Legacy'' (2006) 16]]</ref>

[[File:OwenBeruLars-NEGTC.png|thumb|180px|Beru with her husband, Owen]]
Beru would carry Skywalker with her when she visited Anchorhead to buy supplies, unaware that Kenobi was keeping watch,<ref name="[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]" /> but the Larses eventually came to know that he was constantly checking on Skywalker, though they agreed that it would be best if they all ignored him. Beru played and laughed with Skywalker as a toddler, and as he grew older she would impart to him the values of patience and compassion.<ref name="The Last of the Jedi: The Desperate Mission">''[[The Last of the Jedi: The Desperate Mission]]''</ref><ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> All the while, Beru kept busy on the farm, maintaining the [[Hydroponics/Legends|hydroponics]] labs and coming up with dishes made from roots and herbs to feed the family.<ref name="CCG1">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Beru Lars}}</ref><ref name="Beru Stew">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Beru Stew}}</ref> [[WED-15-77/Legends|WED-15-77]], a [[WED Treadwell repair droid/Legends|WED Treadwell repair droid]] in the family's service, preferred working for Beru because of the same predictable tasks she always gave it.<ref name="Databank3">{{DB|droid|wedtreadwell|WED Treadwell droid}}</ref> Years of daily exposure to Tatooine's [[Binary star/Legends|twin suns]] caused Beru's face to betray her true age.<ref name="Visual Guide">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/explore/visualguides/chp08.html|text=Visual Guide &mdash; Chapter 8: Droids for Sale}}</ref>

As Skywalker matured, Beru and Owen tried to downplay to him things having to do with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. When Skywalker was around six years old, Beru lost a small [[Screwdriver/Legends|screwdriver]] that she used to repair her mending stitcher. Skywalker simply told them that it was under their couch. Owen yelled at the boy for this, but he claimed that it was because Skywalker had to have placed it there himself.<ref name="Children of the Jedi">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> Another time, Skywalker inquired about the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], whom he heard about from someone at [[school]]. Owen dismissed the idea as fiction, but Beru told him while the stories of them were exaggerated, the Jedi did indeed once exist.<ref name="Star Wars Journal: The Fight for Justice">''[[Star Wars Journal: The Fight for Justice]]''</ref>

When Beru wasn't tending to Skywalker or the farm, she enjoyed having friends and relatives visit the homestead from time to time, such as her sister Dama Brunk, [[Windy Starkiller's father|Mister]] and [[Windy Starkiller's mother|Mrs. Starkiller]], and others.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /><ref name="Databank" /> Skywalker's friends frequented too, like [[Camie Loneozner|Camie]], [[Windy Starkiller]], and [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]] and his cousin [[Gavin Darklighter|Gavin]]; they would all later remember Beru fondly.<ref name="Camie's Story" /><ref name="X-Wing: Rogue Squadron">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref>

{{Talesstart}}
When Skywalker began to inquire about his real father, Owen punished the boy, and prevented him from visiting his friends in Anchorhead. Beru felt that Owen was being far too harsh, and that Skywalker's curiosity was only natural. Skywalker sneaked out anyway, and got caught in a dangerous sandstorm. He came down with [[dust fever]], which his Aunt Beru had warned him he was prone to. After hallucinating an adventure with a young boy named "Annie," Skywalker managed to make his way back home.<ref name="Sandstorm">{{Tales|15|Sandstorm (comic story)}}</ref>
{{Talesend}}

[[File:Lars_walkabout.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Beru regrets Owen's attitude towards Ben Kenobi.]]
Beru helped Skywalker recover from his serious bout of dust fever, staying with him for days, feeding him and keeping his temperature down.<ref name="Star Wars Journal: The Fight for Justice" /> At times, she would sing to him an old song about the persistence of love.<ref name="Planet of Twilight">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref>

After keeping his distance for so many years, Kenobi finally encountered Skywalker face-to-face when the boy and his friend Windy Starkiller were caught in a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon's]] cave while seeking shelter from a sandswirl. Kenobi immediately took the boys home, and Beru and the Starkillers were very grateful. However, Owen was furious at Kenobi, and forced the man away from their home, despite Beru's pleas.<ref name="Luke Skywalker's Walkabout">{{StoryCite|story=Luke Skywalker's Walkabout|book=Dark Horse Presents Annual 1999: DHP Jr.}}</ref>

When Skywalker neared eighteen years of age and his friend, Biggs Darklighter, prepared to leave Tatooine for the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]], Darklighter stayed a few nights at the Lars house. While Darklighter ate dinner with the family, Beru asked him about his plans and suggested that Skywalker would likely follow in his footsteps. Owen lashed out at Luke for the idea, including bashing his fist on the table, which upset his nephew considerably.<ref name="Star Wars: Empire 8: Darklighter, Part 1">[[Empire 8|''Empire'' 8]]</ref> When Skywalker planned to go to a farewell party for Darklighter, Owen refused. Beru then reminded her husband that he had let [[Edern Lars/Legends|his brother]] leave without saying goodbye, and so he reluctantly rescinded.<ref name="Star Wars 17: Crucible">[[Star Wars (1977) 17|''Star Wars'' (1977) 17]]</ref> Still, the issue of Skywalker applying for the Academy himself continued to persist. Owen insisted that he needed Skywalker's help for another season, so Beru proposed a compromise: if Skywalker stayed for one last season, Owen would save up and prepare to hire help to replace him.<ref name="Camie's Story" /> Still, while Beru understood how greatly Skywalker wanted to move on, she was pleased that he would be around for a while more.<ref name="Fact File 56">{{FactFile|56|LAR 5-8|Owen and Beru Lars}}</ref>

===Death===
One day in the year following Darklighter's departure, [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Skywalker convinced Owen to invite the [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] to the farm so that they could purchase some new [[Droid/Legends|droids]].<ref name="Fact File 56" /> Beru made certain they knew that if they purchased a [[Translator droid/Legends|translator droid]], it needed to be able to speak [[Bocce/Legends|Bocce]]. Owen purchased two droids&mdash;an [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]], [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], and, coincidentally, C-3PO. As Skywalker cleaned up the newly purchased droids, he discovered that R2-D2 was carrying an important message for Ben Kenobi. When he mentioned this to his aunt and uncle at dinner, Owen dissuaded him from pursuing that particular lead, claiming that Kenobi was just a "crazy old man." Disappointed, Skywalker changed the topic of discussion to his attending the Imperial Academy, but Owen once again asserted that he needed the young man's help for one more year. When Skywalker had departed, Beru tried to convince Owen that it was time to let Skywalker go. That night, Skywalker found that R2-D2 had escaped the farm in pursuit of Kenobi.<ref name="A New Hope" />

[[File:Vaderguide.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Darth Vader orders the execution of Beru and Owen Lars.]]
Early the next morning, Skywalker went after the R2 unit after telling his Aunt Beru that he had some things to do. While Beru prepared breakfast, Owen came looking for the boy, so she relayed what Skywalker had said.<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novel]]</ref> The Larses were likely planning to attend the wedding of [[Eyvind/Legends|Eyvind]] and [[Ariela]] that day, but they never got the chance.<ref name="Drawing the Maps of Peace: The Moisture Farmer's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Drawing the Maps of Peace: The Moisture Farmer's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> While they went about their day, a [[Zeta Squadron (Desert Sands)|group]] of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] led by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Mod Terrik]] showed up, searching for the pair of droids, which carried a stolen set of [[Death Star plans/Legends|top secret plans]]. The troopers laid waste to the Lars home, bringing Beru to tears. Owen cooperated with Terrik, albeit defiantly, but the troopers showed no compassion.<ref name="When the Desert Wind Turns: The Stormtrooper's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=When the Desert Wind Turns: The Stormtrooper's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> Terrik then contacted Darth Vader personally. Vader ordered the Larses killed and watched their execution via [[Hologram/Legends|holoimage]], satisfied to have revenge for their "repeated weaknesses."<ref name="Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader">''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

Meanwhile, Skywalker had found the droids and spent the day with Ben Kenobi. En route to Anchorhead, the group spotted smoke; it was coming from a destroyed Jawa [[Sandcrawler/Legends|sandcrawler]], the one owned by the Jawas that had sold the droids to the Larses.<ref name="Star Wars Journal: The Fight for Justice" /> When Skywalker and Kenobi determined that Imperials were after the droids, Skywalker rushed back home, only to find the homestead ablaze and his aunt and uncle murdered, their charred [[Bone/Legends|skeletal]] remains outside the entrance of their home.<ref name="A New Hope" /> Skywalker buried the only parents he knew<ref name="Legacy 39">[[Legacy (2006) 39|''Legacy'' (2006) 39]]</ref> before departing alongside Kenobi into a trip that would change [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="A New Hope" />

===Legacy===
A short time after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Skywalker returned to Tatooine alongside [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and buried his aunt and uncle outside their home. Skywalker placed a small pendant of Beru when she was young over her burial plot.<ref name="Star Wars 7">[[Star Wars (2013) 7|''Star Wars'' (2013) 7]]</ref> The gravestones for Owen and Beru were still present outside the homestead by [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies" /> Rumors emerged among the community; some thought it was Tuskens that attacked the Lars house, and that Skywalker was killed along with them.<ref name="Star Wars 31: Return to Tatooine">[[Star Wars (1977) 31|''Star Wars'' (1977) 31]]</ref> Others said that it was Skywalker himself who murdered them.<ref name="Camie's Story" /> A later plot by [[Kuat (person)|Kuat of Kuat]] would even try to implicate [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun's]] [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] in their deaths.<ref name="Hard Merchandise">''[[Hard Merchandise]]''</ref> But [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] historian [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] would ensure that Beru was remembered as a woman who loved Skywalker and "helped shape the man that became a galactic hero."<ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook" />

More than a hundred years after her death, Beru appeared in a dream to one of Skywalker's descendants, [[Cade Skywalker]], who had abandoned his heritage and turned into a [[Death stick/Legends|death stick]]-addicted [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]]. In [[137 ABY]], Cade visited Tatooine and, while evading a sandstorm in the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]], stumbled across the abandoned Lars homestead. While resting there, he experienced a dream of Luke Skywalker and him at a dinner in the Lars family, with both Owen and Beru Lars being present and treating Cade as if he had been raised by them alongside Luke. During Cade's imaginary conversation with his ancestor, the dream suddenly changed into the image of the burned homestead and the charred remains of Owen and Beru Lars. Luke then commented on how he failed to understand how much the Larses protected and loved him until it was too late to tell them. He then proceeded his conversation with Cade about the consequences of the latter's actions.<ref name="Legacy 39" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Luke's Aunt Beru, a wonderful lady [&hellip;]|[[Camie Loneozner]]|<ref name="Camie's Story" />}}
[[File:Lars_kitchen.png|thumb|left|300px|Beru Whitesun Lars was a skilled chef and hard worker]]
Beru Whitesun Lars was a Human woman with [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], brown hair<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> worn in a simple style,<ref name="SWCE" /> and fair skin who stood 1.65 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> She favored rough, simple [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] made locally in Anchorhead, such as [[Desert tunic|tunics]] and [[Desert boots|boots]] suitable for [[Desert/Legends|desert]] life.<ref name="SWCE" /> She was well loved by all who knew her.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /><ref name="X-Wing: Rogue Squadron" /> She was not a terribly brilliant woman<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)" /> but was kind, caring, and compassionate towards others. Beru also had a playful side; she and Owen's father, Cliegg, were known to engage in verbal sparring at times.<ref name="Fact File 25">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 25|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 25]]</ref> Beru was an experienced chef,<ref name="Beru Stew" /> cooking most of her family's meals<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)" /> and specializing in preparing different meals utilizing ingredients native to the Tatooinian wastes such as [[giju stew]]<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth">''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth]]''</ref> or [[Beru Stew]], one of several recipes of her own invention.<ref name="Beru Stew" /> She also used to play with her nephew, Luke Skywalker.<ref name="The Last One Standing" />

As part of the fourth generation of moisture farmers of the Whitesun family, considered the family best conditioned to the harsh conditions of the profession,<ref name="Databank" /> Beru had a strong work ethic and was considered an excellent wife for Owen by those around him.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones (novel)" /> Although she supported the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="SWCE" /> Beru was uninterested in traveling offworld. Content in her life on Tatooine,<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones (novel)" /> she proudly worked alongside her husband on the farm season after season,<ref name="Databank" /> tending to the homestead's hydroponics lab personally.<ref name="Beru Stew" /> When the family was low on money, Beru never complained and asked for little from her husband. In fact, her only large request was a droid that spoke Bocce to help her around the house.<ref name="Databank" /> She loved her husband Owen dearly, as did she her nephew, who was essentially her son.<ref name="Fact File 56" />

While her husband would accost Skywalker whenever he would become curious about the Jedi or show signs of his strong Force-sensitivity, Beru was more lenient when dealing with these situations. She would admit, in small amounts, that there was truth to stories her nephew had heard of swashbuckling warriors who once fought for peace among the galaxy.<ref name="Star Wars Journal: The Fight for Justice" /> When it came to Obi-Wan Kenobi, Beru was outwardly much more grateful to the Jedi Master than Owen, who saw completely isolating Skywalker from the "old wizard" as the best means of protecting their nephew,<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)" /> even after Kenobi saved the boy's life from a Krayt Dragon and earned Beru's gratitude.<ref name="Luke Skywalker's Walkabout" /> Beru quietly disliked when Owen raved against Skywalker's protector, but did not stop him.<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)" />

Beru's presence would often cool the confrontions between her husband and nephew and did her best to stop them from colliding head-on.<ref name=" Tyrant's Test" /> which worsened especially in the later years of her life.<ref name="Tyrant's Test">''[[Tyrant's Test]]''</ref> Beru was also more understanding of Skywalker's dreams, such as his wish to join the Imperial Academy, than Owen. She quietly advocated for Skywalker's cause when speaking with her husband<ref name="CCG1" /> and was the one who suggested that Skywalker stay at the homestead for one last season before leaving for the Academy so Owen could raise enough credits to hire someone to replace him, placating both her nephew and husband with the arrangement.<ref name="Camie's Story" /> Although Beru wanted Skywalker around as much as Owen did,<ref name="Fact File 56" /> and respected her husband's desire to stop Skywalker following in his father's footsteps,<ref name="SWCE" /> she also knew that Skywalker needed to get away and pursue his passions.<ref name="Fact File 56" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Aunt Beru, the wife of Owen Lars, raised Luke Skywalker as her own after his mother died and father went off the deep end. She's more than an adoptive parent and a moisture farmer, she's one of the few adults who puts up with Luke's constant pining for the Academy.|[[Bonnie Burton]]|<ref name="SWArchive-Checklist: 10 Unlikely Unleashed Figures">{{SWArchive|url=collecting/news/hasbro/f20071205/index.html|text=Checklist: 10 Unlikely Unleashed Figures|author=[[Bonnie Burton]]|date=2007-12-05}}</ref>}}
[[File:Beru.jpg|thumb|left|Shelagh Fraser as Beru]]
The character of Beru Lars has existed in one form or another since the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of "''The Star Wars''" in [[1974]]. In this draft, Beru and Owen Lars are anthropologists; there is also a character named "[[Clieg Whitsun]]." In the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|1975 version of the script]], the Larses own a moisture ranch, but they are the parents of Skywalker's cousin, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]]. In a later version of this story, Beru protects Skywalker from violent outburst by Owen. However, by an early [[1976]] version, the character is finalized and the element of the Larses being killed by Imperial stormtroopers is added.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>

British actress [[Shelagh Fraser]] was cast to play Aunt Beru in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']]. Fraser's first day of shooting was [[April 1]], 1976; the shots of the Lars' charred skeletons were filmed a few days prior. When post-production on the film began, sound mixer Derek Ball traveled to Fraser's house and recorded additional dialogue.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film" /> In the mono soundmix of the first release of ''Star Wars'', different takes for Beru's lines were used. All subsequent home video sound mixes use the same take that was used in the initial theatrical Dolby mixes.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.in70mm.com/news/2003/star_wars/index.htm|text=The Original First-Week Engagements Of "Star Wars"|archivedate=20070825074407}}</ref>

In the [[1981]] [[National Public Radio]] [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]] adapted by [[Brian Daley]] and directed by [[John Madden]], Beru was voiced by [[Anne Gerety]].

A character biography found in one of the screen savers from the ''[[Star Wars Screen Entertainment]]'' from 1994 lists Beru's maiden name as "Beru Weth," a name contradicted in later sources.

[[File:BeruWhitesunLars.jpg|thumb|right|Bonnie Piesse as Beru]]
On [[July 7]], [[2000]], [[StarWars.com]] announced that sixteen-year-old Australian actress [[Bonnie Maree Piesse|Bonnie Piesse]] would be playing the role of a younger Beru in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|Episode II]].<ref name="Casting">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/production/news20000707.html|text=Casting Update: More Local Talent}}</ref> Piesse would approach Beru as being a little shy, the idea being that it was the introduction of Luke into her life that matured her.<ref name="Insider3">{{InsiderCite|58|Bonnie Piesse: Micro Beru}}</ref> [[George Lucas]] wanted to make sure that Beru's costume was similar to the one worn in the first film to help establish a visual connection.<ref name="Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones">''[[Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> Her wardrobe was also partially inspired by that of Skywalker's friend Camie in ''A New Hope''.<ref name="Databank" /> The first time fans would hear the name "Beru ''Whitesun''" was in [[September]] 2000, when [[Lucasfilm]] began registering [[Wikipedia:Domain name|domain names]] featuring names of characters and other things from the upcoming film.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/episode2/story/lucasfilm_registers_new_episode_ii_domain_names_75320.asp|text=Lucasfilm registers new (Episode II?) domain names!|archivedate=20171006022458}}</ref> This same month, Piesse and the crew were filming the Tatooine scenes in [[Tunisia]].<ref name="Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones" /> Lucas also filmed part of a scene for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|Episode III]] in which a stand-in actor playing Obi-Wan delivers baby Luke to Owen, played by [[Joel Edgerton]]. However, this would be changed during the Episode III shoot in September [[2003]]. Lucas filmed [[Ewan McGregor]] handing the baby to Piesse, with Owen being played by a stand-in&mdash;Edgerton would be shot and added in almost a year later. Lucas made this change because he "felt it would be better if Luke were handed over to a woman."<ref name="The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>

===Deleted scenes===
At least one shot of Beru didn't make the final [[1977]] cut of ''Star Wars'': before the family dinner scene, there is a shot of Beru filling a pitcher of [[Blue milk/Legends|blue milk]] from a dispenser in a portion of the kitchen not visible in the film.<ref name="Lost Cut">{{InsiderCite|41|The Evolution of Star Wars: Exploring the Lost Cut|The Evolution of ''Star Wars'': Exploring the Lost Cut}}</ref> Also, a popular production still from the film reveals that the dinner scene was shot, or at least rehearsed, with the family members sitting in different seats than in the film.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://starwarz.com/tbone/life-on-tatooine|text=Life on Tatooine: The Lars Homestead|archivedate=20190930083346}}</ref>

A more substantial Beru scene was cut from ''Attack of the Clones'': after Anakin Skywalker returns to the farm with his mother's body, Beru helps Amidala prepare a meal, featuring blue milk, for Skywalker, having a short conversation with Amidala about Naboo and her own reluctance to travel. Nonetheless, this scene does appear in the film's [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization]].<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://starwarz.com/tbone/return-to-tatooine|text=Return To Tatooine: Beru Whitesun|archivedate=20200727193242}}</ref> A shot of Beru and the Larses waving goodbye to Anakin and Padmé was also shot but not used in the final film.<ref name="Y'all">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/explore/attack/2002/07/imageattack20020723.html|series=Image Attack|text=Y'all Come Back Now}}</ref>

===Non-canon content===
===="Old Wounds"====
{{Quote|Beru, bring me the rifle.''"<br />"''Owen, what is it? Tusken Raider?''"<br />"''Don't think so. It looks to be alone.|Owen and Beru, after Darth Maul runs towards the Lars farm|<ref name="Old Wounds">{{StoryCite|story=Old Wounds|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>}}
[[File:OldWoundsCharacters.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Beru crawls towards Owen while Maul and Kenobi duel.]]
Beru appears in the [[2005]]<ref name="Old Wounds" /> [[canon|non-canon]]<ref name="SWBoards">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=125719&start=0675#10095628|thread=Event Timeline and Character Age Discussion|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2005-03-29|time=11:02 AM}}</ref> comic "[[Old Wounds]]," written and illustrated by [[Aaron McBride]] and published in the anthology ''[[Star Wars: Visionaries]]''.<ref name="Old Wounds" /> In [[16 BBY/Legends|16 BBY]],<ref name="Old Wounds Date">The opening panel of "[[Old Wounds]]" places the events of the comic in the third [[Standard year/Legends|year]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] occupation of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], which took place in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Therefore, "Old Wounds" must be set in [[16 BBY/Legends|16 BBY]].</ref> Owen and Luke were watching the sunset on the farm when Owen saw a [[Sith apparel|robed]] figure with [[Metal/Legends|metallic]] legs, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], sprinting towards them. Owen called for Beru to bring his [[GRS-1 snare rifle/Legends|rifle]] out, as she did she asked if it was a Tusken Raider, which Owen doubted as the figure was alone. He ordered Beru to take Luke inside, but she stayed out. Owen fired at Maul, but the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] knocked him down.<ref name="Old Wounds" />

Beru, still holding Luke, begged Maul not to harm them. At that point, Maul [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] Kenobi's presence and began calling out to him, as the Jedi was his true quarry whom he sought revenge on for [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|taking]] his legs. After Maul recounted his journey to Tatooine, as he knew threatening Luke would draw Kenobi out, the Jedi burst from under the ground and the two began to [[Duel at the Lars homestead|duel]]. Beru continued holding Luke as she crawled towards Owen during the [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]] to check on his welfare. Eventually, the duel ended with Owen killing Maul when Kenobi was unable to do so. Beru held Luke as Owen and Kenobi discussed their agreement to keep Luke safe, with Owen prohibiting the Jedi from returning to the farm.<ref name="Old Wounds" /> Still Kenobi reassured Luke through the force that even if he could not see him, he would always be with Luke in spirit.
